# Pericardiocentesis

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Cardiology and angiology > Pericardial diseases > Pericardiocentesis*

[Original Article Link](/library/WF0PS3)

---

## Summary

Pericardiocentesis is a procedure that involves removing <u>pericardial</u> fluid for diagnostic evaluation or to treat <u>pericardial effusions</u> and/or <u>cardiac tamponade</u>. It may be performed in both children and adults.A <u>spinal needle</u> is attached to a syringe and inserted into the <u>pericardial sac</u> to <u>aspirate</u> blood or fluid. A temporary drain may be placed during the procedure if significant <u>pericardial fluid drainage</u> is required. Multiple approaches (subxiphoid, apical, and parasternal) may be used to perform pericardiocentesis, generally with <u>ultrasound</u> guidance. There are no <u>absolute contraindications</u> to pericardiocentesis. Complications include <u>dysrhythmias</u>, <u>pneumothorax</u>, <u>pneumopericardium</u>, and <u>pericardial decompression syndrome</u>.
